info.title: backend
info.description: 12-factor Rust backend: layered store + RBAC + JWT + WS + worker

409.description: Conflict — address is used by schedules

get.summary:
`GET /api/admin/chat/stats` — aggregate chat stats for the admin
dashboard's top-row cards.
get.description:
Returns counts of channels grouped by status (open / assigned /
closed / total) + the average first-response time in seconds.

Server-side aggregate so the counts are accurate even when there
are more channels than the channel list's page size (capped at 200).

Generates a CSRF state, stores it in a cookie, and 302-redirects

post.summary: `POST /api/auth/refresh` — rotate refresh token, issue new access.
post.description:
Reads the refresh token from the httpOnly cookie first (preferred —
the token never touches JS), then falls back to the request body
(for non-browser clients).

post.description:
Issues auth cookies immediately on success so the user doesn't need to
call `/login` separately.

post.summary: `POST /api/bookings` and `POST /api/bookings/hold` — hold seats for a booking.

get.summary: `GET /api/bookings/lookup` — lookup a booking by phone or code.
`GET /api/chat/channels` — list chat channels for the authenticated user.
get.description:
For **customers**: returns only their own channels (the ones they started).
For **employees**: returns the entire open-channel support queue (optionally
filtered by the employee's brand) so support staff see all inbound chats.

Each channel includes the customer's `user` row (`id`, `fullName`,
`email`, `phone`, `avatarUrl`) so the admin's channel list can
display "who" without a second round-trip per channel.

post.summary:
`POST /api/chat/channels` — create a new chat channel for the
authenticated user.

get.description:
Returns messages in **DESC order (newest first)** to support
cursor pagination. The frontend reverses the page before rendering
so the oldest message is at the top + the newest at the bottom
(the natural chat reading order).

- `limit` defaults to 30 (modern chat default — fast first paint).
  Max 200.
- `offset` defaults to 0. `offset=30` returns the next 30 OLDER
  messages.

When a new message arrives via WS, the frontend invalidates this
query so the latest page refetches with the new message at the
top of the DESC page (which becomes the bottom after the
frontend reverses it).

post.summary:
`POST /api/chat/channels/{id}/messages` — REST fallback for posting
a chat message.
post.description:
Auth required: the caller must be the channel's owner (user side)
or an employee. Idempotent via `client_msg_id`.

**WS broadcast**: after the message is persisted, we broadcast a
`message` event to the channel room so the OTHER side (customer or
admin) sees the reply in realtime without needing to refetch. We
ALSO broadcast a `channel_message` event to ALL online employees
(admin attention signal) when the sender is a customer.

If the request body's `ids` array is empty, ALL of the user's unread
notifications are marked read. Otherwise only the listed ids are
marked (ownership-checked — ids not owned by the caller are ignored).

get.description:
**Authorization**: requires the `ADMIN_NULLCLAW_READ` permission
(any employee/support role). The exchanges contain the customer's
original prompt + the AI's completion, which may include PII such
as phone numbers, booking codes, and travel plans. Exposing them
publicly would be a data-leak (OWASP API1:2023 BOLA / API2:2023
Excessive Data Exposure).

post.summary: `POST /api/payments` — initiate a payment for a booking.

post.description:
MoMo POSTs JSON to `ipnUrl`. We verify the HMAC-SHA256 signature
over the canonical alphabetical-key string. Response: HTTP 204
with body `{"code":0,"message":"..."}`.

get.description:
VNPay POSTs the IPN as a GET request (with all params in the URL).
We re-verify the HMAC-SHA512 signature and transition the payment state.
Response body must be JSON `{"RspCode":"00","Message":"Confirm Success"}`.

post.description:
ZaloPay POSTs JSON; the `mac` field is HMAC-SHA256 over the raw body
bytes. We must read the body as raw bytes BEFORE deserialising to
avoid the JSON normaliser reformatting it (any byte-level difference
breaks the MAC).

The route handler:
  1. Reads the raw body bytes.
  2. Re-deserialises them to `ZalopayCallbackPayload`.
  3. Passes both the parsed struct + raw bytes to the service.

400.description: Payment is not in pending status

post.summary:
`POST /api/payments/{id}/mark-cod-collected` — driver / admin marks
that cash was physically received for a COD booking.

400.description: Not a COD payment or not pending

AdminBookingDetail.description: Admin booking detail — full shape with seats.

total.description:
Total matching-row count (independent of pagination). Omitted when
the server didn't compute it (older callers may rely on this).

AdminBookingOut.description: Admin booking list item — slim shape for the table view.

previousStatus.description:
The original requested status (before normalization). Useful
when the caller sends `paid` and we store `confirmed`.

AdminBrandOut.description: Admin brand list item — like `BrandOut` but with `routeCount` + `layoutCount`.

AdminPaymentOut.description:
Admin-flavoured `PaymentOut` — same fields, plus a few admin-only
extras (booking code + provider response blob).

bookingCode.description:
Joined from the booking row — the human-readable booking code
(e.g. `VEXEVN-AB12CD`). Lets the admin list / search without an
extra round-trip per row.

id.description:
City slug (e.g. `"ha-noi"`). NOT a UUID — matches the
`start_location_id` / `end_location_id` column type on `route`.

AdminRouteOut.description:
Admin route list item — like `RouteOut` but with start/end place
previews and schedule/pickup-point counts.

startLocationId.description:
City slug (e.g. `"ha-noi"`). Required — every route has both a
start and an end city. Resolved to `start_location` via
`crate::cities::find_by_slug`.

busLayoutId.description:
Bus layout id (string on the wire, `Uuid` in Rust — see the
entity field comment about the old String/TEXT drift).

points.description:
Ordered address points (departure → midway stops → destination).
Empty when the schedule has no point sequence yet.

BankTransferInstructions.description: Manual bank-transfer instructions for the VietQR flow.

memo.description:
Memo to include in the transfer — embeds the booking code so the
reconciliation script can match incoming transfers to bookings.

BookingListItem.description:
Response of `GET /api/bookings` (list item) and `GET /api/bookings/{id}`
(detail — same shape, just with the full trip preview filled in).

paidAt.description: Timestamp when the booking was paid (`updated_at` snapshot at status=confirmed).

total.description:
Total matching-row count (independent of pagination). Omitted from
the JSON when the server didn't compute it (e.g. for the lookup
endpoint). Use `with_total(...)` to set it.

BookingLookupResponse.description:
Response of `GET /api/bookings/lookup`. Same shape as the list, but
without the `total` field (the lookup endpoint doesn't paginate).

BookingSeatOut.description: A held seat inside a booking response.

brandAccent.description: Present on the booking-list payload (not the detail payload).

brandLogo.description: Present on the booking-list payload (not the detail payload).

brandName.description: Present on the booking-list payload (not the detail payload).

oneOf.description: Present on the detail payload (not the list payload).

pickupPoints.description: Present on the detail payload (not the list payload).

oneOf.description: Present on the detail payload (not the list payload).

routeName.description: Present on the booking-list payload (not the detail payload).

vehicleType.description: Present on the booking-list payload (not the detail payload).

discount.description: Discount amount (VND) applied to the subtotal. 0 when invalid.

ChannelUserOut.description:
The customer who started the channel. Embedded in [`ChatChannelOut`]
so the admin's channel list can display name / email / phone without
a second round-trip per channel.

ChatChannelOut.description:
A chat channel, as returned by `GET /api/chat/channels` and the
create-channel endpoint.

oneOf.description:
The customer who started the channel. Populated by `list_channels`
+ `create_channel` (joined from the `user` table by `user_id`).

`None` only when the user has been deleted (FK CASCADE clears
the channel row, so this is rare).

ChatMessageOut.description:
A chat message, as returned by `GET /api/chat/channels/{id}/messages`
and the post-message endpoint.

ChatStatsResponse.description:
Response of `GET /api/admin/chat/stats` — aggregate chat stats for
the admin dashboard's top-row cards.

- `openCount` — channels with `status='open'` (the support queue).
- `assignedCount` — channels with `status='assigned'` (being handled).
- `closedCount` — channels with `status='closed'` (resolved).
- `totalChannels` — sum of all statuses.
- `avgResponseTimeSecs` — average seconds between the first user
  message + the first employee reply, across channels that have
  both. `0.0` when no channels have a response yet.

CreateChannelRequest.description: Request body for `POST /api/chat/channels` (create a new chat channel).

CreateMessageRequest.description:
Request body for `POST /api/chat/channels/{id}/messages` (REST
fallback for when the WebSocket is unavailable).

CreatePaymentReq.description:
Request body for `POST /api/payments` — initiate a payment for a booking.

The `provider` field selects which gateway to use:
- `vnpay`, `momo`, `zalopay` → user is redirected to the gateway's hosted
  checkout page. The gateway then redirects back to the app + sends an
  IPN webhook to confirm.
- `vietqr` → server generates an EMV QR string; user scans it with their
  banking app to transfer funds. Confirmation is manual (admin
  reconciliation) or via a future H2H bank webhook.
- `cod` → cash-on-boarding. No gateway interaction. Booking is held
  until the driver/agent marks cash as collected.

bookingId.description: Booking id to pay for. Must be in `pending` status (not yet confirmed).

provider.description:
One of: `vnpay` | `momo` | `zalopay` | `vietqr` | `cod`.
Validated against the entity's allow-list.

CreatePriceAlertRequest.description:
`POST /api/price-alerts` request body.

Accepts both `targetPrice` (canonical) and `maxPrice` (legacy alias
used by some frontend hooks) — the route normalizes to `targetPrice`.

CreatePriceAlertResponse.description:
`POST /api/price-alerts` response. Includes a `duplicate` flag so the
frontend can show "alert already exists" feedback.

CreateReviewInput.description:
Input for creating a review. Field names on the wire are camelCase
(so the frontend can send `{ bookingId, routeId, brandId, rating, ... }`)
but the Rust struct uses snake_case.

userId.description: Overwritten by the server from the authenticated user.

schedulerEnabled.description:
Whether the background-jobs subsystem (worker runner + scheduler
tick) is running in this process. `false` (SCHEDULER_ENABLED=false)
→ schedules won't fire and triggering returns 503.

CronJobOut.description: A scheduled (recurring) job, with its latest run attached.

atHour.description: Local wall-clock hour (0-23) of the fire time.

atMinute.description: Local wall-clock minute (0-59) of the fire time.

description.description:
Human-readable description from the job catalog (absent for
operator-inserted custom rows).

oneOf.description:
Latest run, any status — doubles as the live status of an
in-flight run (started + not finished).

nextRunAt.description: Next fire time (ISO-8601 UTC). `None` when never armed.

CronJobRunOut.description: One execution of a background job — history / live status row.

detail.description: Progress / stats JSON (phase, message, bytes, indexed counts…).

activeConnections.description:
Current active connections (in use). `-1` if unavailable
(e.g. SQLite which doesn't have a pool).

idleConnections.description: Current idle connections (in pool, available). `-1` if unavailable.

sizeMb.description:
Database file size in MB (SQLite only — WAL + main DB file).
`0.0` for Postgres (no file).

DirectionsResponse.description:
Turn-by-turn driving directions.

Returned by `GET /api/routing/directions`. The `valhalla` field
carries the raw Valhalla `trip` object (kept opaque — different
Valhalla versions emit slightly different shapes; we expose the
top-level summary fields the UI cares about).

shape.description: Encoded polyline of the route, if Valhalla returned one.

valhalla.description: Raw Valhalla `trip` object (opaque — passed through as-is).

IpnResponse.description:
Generic response shape returned by all IPN handlers. Different
providers expect different bodies — the route handler converts this
into the provider-specific response.

code.description:
Provider-specific success code (e.g. `"00"` for VNPay, `0` for MoMo,
`1` for ZaloPay).

IsochroneResponse.description:
Reachability polygons (isochrones).

Returned by `GET /api/routing/isochrone`. The `geojson` field is
the raw Valhalla isochrone response (a FeatureCollection of polygons
— one per contour time).

total.description:
Total matching-row count (independent of pagination). Omitted
when the endpoint doesn't paginate (e.g. booking-detail lookup).

Total post count (independent of pagination). Omitted when not
computed.

MarkCodCollectedReq.description:
Request body for `POST /api/payments/{id}/mark-cod-collected`.
Driver / admin marks that cash was physically received for a COD booking.

amountCollected.description:
Optional: amount actually collected (VND integer). Defaults to the
payment's recorded amount. Useful if the driver collected partial cash.

ids.description:
Notification ids to mark as read. When empty, ALL of the user's
unread notifications are marked read.

MatrixResponse.description:
Many-to-many travel time / distance matrix.

Returned by `GET /api/routing/matrix`. `timesMin[i][j]` is the
travel time (in minutes) from source `i` to target `j`;
`distancesKm[i][j]` is the distance in km. `None` cells mean
Valhalla could not route between that pair.

NotificationOut.description: A notification row, as returned by `GET /api/notifications`.

data.description:
Optional JSON-encoded payload (e.g. the booking id for a
booking_confirmed notification).

NullclawExchangeOut.description:
A single NullClaw exchange row — the prompt + completion pair, with
metadata (model used, latency, handoff flag).

type.description:
`adult` | `child` | `infant`. Serialized as `type` on the wire
(matches the legacy field name the frontend sends).

PaymentOut.description:
A single payment row, with provider-specific rendering hints.

Front-end rendering rules:
- `gatewayUrl` is set → render a "Pay now" button that opens the URL
  in a new tab. Used by VNPay/MoMo/ZaloPay.
- `qrPayload` is set → render a QR image (encode the payload string with
  any client-side QR library, or call the `qr-image` endpoint). Used by
  VietQR.
- Neither is set + `provider == "cod"` → render "Pay on the bus" copy
  + "Cash collected by driver" status pill. Used by COD.

oneOf.description:
Bank details for the manual-transfer (VietQR) flow. Returned only
when the provider is `vietqr` — used to display "Transfer to: …"
instructions alongside the QR.

collectedAt.description: For COD: when the driver collected the cash.

collectedBy.description: For COD: which admin user marked the payment as collected.

qrImageDataUri.description:
For VietQR: a PNG data URI of the QR image, pre-rendered server-side.
Saves the front-end from pulling a QR library. `qr_payload` is also
returned for clients that want to render their own QR.

qrPayload.description: For VietQR: the EMV QR TLV string (CRC included).

returnUrl.description:
Public URL where the gateway should redirect the user after the
user completes / cancels the payment on the hosted checkout page.
The front-end uses this to build its own "Return to app" button
in case the auto-redirect fails.

PlaceOut.description: A place row from the database, as returned by `GET /api/places`.

type.description:
OSM place kind (city / town / village / suburb ...). Mirrors the
DB column `place.type` (renamed because `type` is a Rust keyword).

PlaceSearchHit.description:
A search hit returned by `GET /api/places/search?q=`.

When the Tantivy index is configured, fields like `osmId`, `ward`,
`district`, `city`, `score`, `distanceKm` are populated. When the
SQL LIKE fallback is used, only the DB-backed fields are set.

distanceKm.description:
Distance from the `lat` / `lon` query param, in km. Set when
the caller passes `lat` + `lon` (geo-bias).

id.description: DB row id (only set when the hit comes from the `place` table).

osmId.description: OSM node/way id (only set for Tantivy hits).

score.description: Tantivy relevance score (0..1). Only set for Tantivy hits.

type.description: `place.type` (DB hits only — present on SQL LIKE fallback).

engine.description:
Which engine produced the results: `tantivy` (fulltext index) or
`sql` (LIKE fallback). Omitted for the SQL fallback.

PriceAlertListEnvelope.description:
Concrete list envelope for price alerts. Registered in the OpenAPI
`components(schemas(...))` (utoipa needs a non-generic type there).
The JSON shape is identical to `ListEnvelope<PriceAlertOut>`.

PriceAlertOut.description:
Price alert as returned to the client. Field names are camelCase
to match the frontend's `PriceAlert` type.

cpuUsage.description:
CPU usage % (0.0–100.0). Sampled over the last refresh interval.
First call after startup may return 0.0 (sysinfo needs two
samples to compute usage).

memoryMb.description: RSS memory in MB (resident set size — actual physical RAM used).

virtualMemoryMb.description:
Virtual memory in MB (total addressable memory, includes
mapped files + shared libraries). Mostly informational.

refresh_token.description:
Optional refresh token in the body. If absent, the token is read
from the `refresh_token` httpOnly cookie. Accepting it from the
body is a fallback for non-browser clients (curl, mobile) that
can't use cookies.

ReviewOut.description: A review row, as returned by `GET /api/reviews` and `GET /api/reviews/{id}`.

ReviewTagsResponse.description:
Response of `GET /api/reviews/tags`. Returns the distinct set of
tags across all reviews (used by the frontend to render tag filters).

RouteOut.description: A route list item returned by `GET /api/routes`.

SessionUser.description:
Identity of an authenticated actor, derived from the `user` row.

`actor_type` is `"user"` for customers and `"employee"` for staff. The
distinction matters for the chat / call hubs (only employees may register
as agents) and for nullclaw (human-fallback threshold counts online
employees).

ToggleWishlistRequest.description:
Request body for `POST /api/wishlist`. Toggles the route in the
user's wishlist — if it's already wishlisted, the existing item is
removed (toggle off); otherwise a new item is created (toggle on).

added.description:
`true` when the route is now in the wishlist; `false` when it was
removed by the toggle.

trip.description:
The trip + nested route + brand + bus layout + pickup points +
seat map + campaigns, all in one response (frontend's
TripDetailDialog consumes it).

TripResult.description:
A trip search result returned by `GET /api/search` and
`GET /api/recommendations`.

maxPrice.description: Same as `min_price` for now (backend doesn't have a max price per trip).

force.description: When `true`, skips the state-machine transition check (admin override).

UpdateCronJobRequest.description:
Body of `PATCH /api/admin/cron-jobs/{jobType}` — all fields optional;
omitted fields keep their current values.

resetNextRun.description: Re-arm the next run from now (uses the schedule's time-of-day).

UpsertBrandRequest.description:
Request body for `POST /api/admin/brands` (create) and
`PUT /api/admin/brands/{id}` (update — all fields optional).

startLocationId.description:
City slug (e.g. `"ha-noi"`). Max 20 chars — matches the DB
column `VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL`. The slug MUST be one of the
values in `crate::cities::CITIES`; we don't enforce that here
(validator doesn't have access to the static list) but the
frontend dropdown only sends known slugs. Required — a route
without start/end cities is meaningless.

UpsertSchedulePointItem.description:
One entry of the ordered `points` array on schedule create/update.
The array position defines `stopOrder`; `kind` is derived
(first = `pickup`, last = `drop`, else `middle`).

busLayoutId.description: Bus layout id (string on the wire, `Uuid` in Rust).

points.description:
When present, replaces the schedule's whole point sequence.
Requires ≥ 2 items (departure + destination); `kind` and
`stopOrder` are derived from the array position.

email.description:
User's email. The underlying column is non-null but may be empty —
we normalise to `None` for the wire so the frontend's optional type
is honest.

connections.description: Total live WS connections (across all users + employees).

distinctIps.description: Distinct client IPs (used for per-IP connection caps).

onlineEmployeeBrands.description:
Number of distinct brands with online employees. The hub
indexes online employees by brand key (`brandId → employeeId →
set<socketId>`). This is the count of brand keys with ≥1
online employee.

onlineEmployees.description:
Total online employees (sum across all brands). Useful for
the admin dashboard — "how many support staff are online?".

rooms.description:
Number of chat rooms (one per open channel that has at least
one joined socket). Empty rooms are cleaned up by the hub GC.

WishlistItemOut.description: A wishlist item, as returned by `GET /api/wishlist`.
